subject: reasoning
question: D, E, F, G, H, I and K are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table. I sits third to the left of H. E sits second to the left of G. Only H sits between D and E. K is not an immediate neighbour of I. How many people sit between F and E when counted from the right of F?
solution:
**Given: **D, E, F, G, H, I and K are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table.

I sits third to the left of H. E sits second to the left of G. Only H sits between D and E.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8775bedeb35489adf4933eac5970b656d9b11ef543143a2377f03fb341dbbd1c.png] 

K is not an immediate neighbour of I. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/336b19e956f1c3b11600f1d91c53d62ecd13373a825f21cc8f10d4160b52c7b5.png] 

Thus, Only two people sit between F and E when counted from the right of F.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 3".**
